title: WTO upgrades goods trade forecast as AI boom offsets Middle East disruption
source_used: Associated Press (text read on Yahoo Finance Canada)
key_facts: The World Trade Organization raised its 2026 forecast for growth in the volume of goods trade to 3.9%, from 1.9% in its spring forecast.
It forecasts 4.1% growth in 2027, up from 2.9% predicted in March.
Goods trade grew 3.5% in the first half of 2026, powered by AI-related spending.
AI-enabling goods such as semiconductors and servers accounted for 47% of global goods trade growth in the first half, and trade in them rose 67% year on year.
Middle East LNG exports fell 47% in the first half and crude oil exports nearly a quarter, but shipments from other suppliers limited the global decline to about 1% for LNG and 6% for crude.
The WTO expects global GDP to grow 2.6% in 2026 and 2.9% in 2027, with the Middle East conflict still weighing on trade through higher energy prices and disrupted routes.
Chief economist Robert Steiger said forecasters were surprised by the strength of the AI investment boom.
quote_evidence: Demand for AI-enabling goods such as semiconductors and servers accounted for 47% of global merchandise trade growth in the first half of 2026, and trade in these products rose by 67% year-on-year
The revision reflects evidence that global supply chains adapted to disruptions in energy and fertilizer markets
why_it_matters_hint: AI hardware demand is now a main driver of world goods trade.
